title: F# Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Print a greeting
examples.description: printfn prints formatted output and a new line. %s stands for text.

examples.title: Keep a named value
examples.description: let gives a name to a value. It cannot be changed unless declared mutable.

examples.title: Name a calculation
examples.description: A function is defined with let and an input name. Its expression is the result.

examples.title: Choose a value
examples.description: if is an expression with then and else results.
examples.code:
let score = 8
let message = if score >= 5 then "Pass" else "Try again"
printfn "%s" message

examples.title: Keep a list
examples.description: List items are separated by semicolons. List.head reads the first item.

examples.title: Transform each value
examples.description: List.map applies a function to every item and returns a new list.
examples.code:
let values = [2; 3] |> List.map (fun n -> n * 2)
printfn "%A" values

examples.title: Keep matching values
examples.description: List.filter keeps values that pass a Boolean test.
examples.code:
let values = [4; 8; 9] |> List.filter (fun n -> n >= 7)
printfn "%A" values

examples.title: Unpack a pair
examples.description: A tuple groups values. Pattern matching can give names to its parts.

examples.title: Group named fields
examples.description: A record has named fields. A new record can copy an old one with one field changed.

examples.title: Handle an absent value
examples.description: An option is Some(value) or None. Pattern matching handles both.
examples.code:
let score: int option = None
let value = match score with | Some n -> n | None -> 0
printfn "%d" value

examples.title: Name a set of cases
examples.description: A union describes a fixed set of cases. match selects an action for a case.
examples.code:
type Light = Red | Green
let light = Green
let message = match light with | Red -> "Stop" | Green -> "Go"
printfn "%s" message

examples.title: Combine list values
examples.description: List.fold carries a result through the list. The starting total is zero here.
examples.code:
let total = [2; 3; 4] |> List.fold (fun sum n -> sum + n) 0
printfn "%d" total
